Subject: Greenbridge: order form settlement schedule, invoicing entity & tax responsibility

Team — looping you all in on Greenbridge's redlines to the Order Form and a short list of asks from procurement attached (Greenbridge_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf). Key commercial points they raised and our suggested positions: 

- Minimum commit phasing: they want to avoid a single upfront invoice. They propose quarterly billing against a single aggregate commit.
- Invoicing entity: they asked to have the UK affiliate billed for EMEA usage — we need to confirm whether we can split invoicing across entities for a single deal.
- Net terms: procurement is pushing Net45; sales prefers Net30.
- Tax responsibility: they flagged VAT reverse-charge and want Redwood to accept VAT liability in some markets.

Can legal/finance run a quick pass on feasibility and redline language? Kimberly — are there MSA implications (jurisdiction/indemnity) if we invoice a non-US affiliate? Ben — from sales, I think we can offer a phased billing compromise. Lauren — finance, can you confirm whether we can support split-entity invoicing operationally and what evidence you need (W-9, VAT docs)?

Goal: I want a one-page proposal we can send back to procurement by EOD Wednesday with a proposed invoicing schedule, net-terms compromise, and list of required tax evidence.

Thanks,
Rishi

Thanks Rishi — quick legal passthrough below. I reviewed the attached redlines. High-level notes: 

- Invoicing entity: we can invoice multiple entities but need the Order Form to map which services are delivered to which legal entity. The current MSA references a single "Customer" with one invoice recipient; splitting requires an explicit schedule and an amendment to the Order Form (not a change to the MSA core language).

- Jurisdiction & indemnity: procurement added a clause shifting certain IP/indemnity risks to Redwood's local entity. We should push back — propose retaining Redwood US/Delaware as governing law and add a limited carve for local tax compliance only.

- Net terms: Net45 is acceptable for enterprise procurement but creates cashflow exposure. If we agree to Net45, request a 25% upfront activation invoice to mitigate risk (or Net30 with no upfront).

- VAT/taxes: we need copies of the buyer's VAT registration and a statement on who is contractually responsible for VAT. If they want Redwood to collect/reverse-charge, provide a template VAT schedule in the Order Form and require procurement to supply certificates.

I can draft the Order Form amendment language today. 

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick from sales perspective — thanks for the review. Proposed compromise I can take to Greenbridge: 

1) Billing split: 50% of the first-year minimum commit billed upfront to Greenbridge, Inc. (US entity) as an activation/invoice. The other 50% will be invoiced in equal quarterly tranches to Greenbridge UK Ltd for EMEA consumption (we'll include a mapping table showing quantity by region).

2) Net terms: offer Net30 on the activation invoice; Net45 on subsequent quarterly invoices if they must have Net45. Alternatively, accept Net45 across the board if they provide a PO and a 25% upfront security retainer (or escrow holdback) that we apply to overdue balances.

3) Taxes: request VAT registration and VAT IDs for the UK entity. If their position is reverse-charge, require a signed VAT declaration and commit language in the Order Form stating customer is responsible for local VAT unless otherwise agreed.

Operational asks for finance: Lauren — can you confirm whether you can accept split remittance and what fields you need on the invoice to route correctly (entity name, remit-to, PO number, VAT ID)? Also list any timing constraints for issuance and payment processing for UK invoices.

If this is acceptable I will present verbatim language and a simple schedule to procurement and ask them to sign off on the amendment.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Director, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

Thanks for the quick responses — appreciate the options. Procurement spoke with finance and below is what Greenbridge can accept: 

- Billing split: we can accept a split as you suggested (50/50) provided you issue the activation invoice to Greenbridge, Inc. (US) and quarterly invoices to Greenbridge UK Ltd. Each invoice must include the PO number and the remit-to details for the billed entity.

- Net terms: Greenbridge legal prefers Net45 for EMEA invoices and Net30 for US invoices. The PO will reflect that. We cannot do a 25% retainer; however, we can put a 30-day escrow holdback for the first two quarters to mitigate risk while we ramp.

- Taxes: attached is our procurement form (GB_Procurement_Form.xlsx) and a request for your W-9 plus the VAT evidence we requested. If Redwood expects Greenbridge to bear VAT, we will need explicit Order Form language to that effect.

Please confirm you can: (a) provide a W-9 and Redwood US invoicing details; (b) accept PO routing by entity; and (c) add the VAT schedule to the Order Form amendment. We will sign once those are in place.
